answers.description: Question id to answer used, incl. defaulted questions; choice/text answers are strings, number answers numbers; empty object when none. Cross-checks against declared questions are validator-level (SPEC 7).

tunables.description: Complete flat tunables map after answer resolution (SPEC 5 resolved tuning snapshot)

constants.description: Package constants; an empty object when the package declares none

scope.description: Exact human-readable statement of what the hash covers

file.description: Package-relative path to the canonical payload bytes

harness.$comment: additionalProperties true by design: build-local checkpoint records, fixtures, and transcripts live here without being core contract (SPEC 7).

split.description: Percentages; validator must additionally check they sum to 100

commerce.description: The manifest's commerce profile, copied verbatim; present only when a commerce split exists to attribute

renderer.description: Optional free-text declaration of the rendering technique this build used, such as "three.js 0.185.1, WebGL" (SPEC 7). The renderer is the builder's fact, never the spec's: SPEC 3's platform names the state space, and two builds of one spec may declare different renderers. Declarative only in v0.5; the web-1 capture recipe does not read it.

id.description: Build-local label for the concrete adapter invocation

kind.description: Closed, versioned enum. web-1 names the headless-browser reference profile summarized in SPEC 7: synthetic-clock deterministic frame capture with a capture-manifest record. Widening this enum is an ordinary additive change.

capture_profile.$comment: capture_profile is distinct from the manifest-level verification_profiles/material-simulation-envelope-1 concept (SPEC 3, SPEC 6a).
capture_profile.description: Optional declaration of which capture adapter and serving/run recipe produced this certification (SPEC 7). Declarative only: does not change acceptance-count or hash-payload rules.

resources.$comment: Resource-id uniqueness is a validator-level check. List presence is a disclosure, not a certified-complete claim (SPEC 7).
resources.description: Optional build-resource provenance disclosure list: kits, third-party assets, and tools the build consumed (SPEC 7). Provenance only: it creates no split obligation and changes no certification outcome.

artifact.description: Names the exact single immutable file or archive hash covers: a URL, a registry coordinate (name@version), or a package-relative path. A multi-file kit, tree, or tool install MUST be packaged into one archive before hashing; v0.5 defines no directory/tree-hash canonicalization.

license.description: Free-text declaration; presence, not truth, is checked

hash.description: Covers exactly the bytes named by artifact

source.description: Optional origin (URL, registry id, or similar), distinct from artifact's exact-bytes identification

directionClaimPath.$comment: This pattern is a necessary, not sufficient, check. A validator-level cross-check (SPEC 7/9.11) additionally MUST resolve every path against the certifying spec's direction.json and reject a path that does not name a declared entry of one of the five fixed-judged kinds (pillars.*, mood.*, anti.*, invariants.*, motion.*). A syntactically well-formed but nonexistent path, such as pillars.not-declared, is a hard failure.
directionClaimPath.description: SPEC 9.10 dotted-path citation of a judged direction claim

status.description: SPEC 9.11 judged gate. pending is the only value v0.5 defines because the panel protocol is not yet integrated into the conformance suite.

assessed.description: Every judged claim this run attempted to assess (coverage-of-claims-assessed, SPEC 9.11). Each path MUST resolve to a declared entry; see directionClaimPath $comment.

adherent.description: The subset of assessed judged as adherent (adherence-over-assessed-claims, SPEC 9.11). A validator-level check requires adherent to be a subset of assessed and requires every path to resolve to a declared entry.

judged.description: Required exactly when the certifying spec's direction.json declares at least one judged claim (pillars/mood/anti/invariants/motion); absent otherwise.

certified_pins.description: SPEC 9.9 descent-rule evidence: the captured resolved value for every constraints.palette.* entry carrying certify: true in the source spec's direction.json. Only direction-constraint palette pins appear here; mood-descriptor palettes cannot carry certify in v0.5. A validator-level cross-check (SPEC 7) requires exactly one entry per certified palette claim and requires value to equal that claim's declared value within ΔE00 = 0. Required exactly when the certifying spec's direction.json declares at least one certify:true constraints.palette.* claim; absent otherwise.

directionResult.description: SPEC 9.11/9.9 direction certification result. Required exactly when the certifying spec's direction.json declares at least one judged claim OR at least one certify:true constraints.palette.* claim. The two conditions are independent: a constraints-only carrier with a certified pin and zero judged claims carries certified_pins with no judged member. Absent when neither condition holds. judged and certified_pins may both be present.
